name: Media and Publishing
title: Editorial evidence and rights coordination
summary: Assemble source verification, asset rights, and publication checks for editor-owned release decisions.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A newsroom prepares a feature that combines interviews, public records, photographs, and syndicated material. Editors need to know which claims are supported and which assets can be used in the planned channels. Agents organize evidence and draft checks; editors retain publication judgment and accountability.
problem: A fluent draft can turn an allegation into a fact, misattribute a quotation, or apply rights granted for one channel to another. Web pages and source documents may also contain malicious instructions intended to redirect research tools.
whyAgents: Claim verification, quotation alignment, rights review, and editorial assembly specialists inspect different evidence. The workflow preserves the exact source passages and licensed asset versions rather than relying on a general model's confidence.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure editorial check coverage and correction burden rather than equating generated volume with quality. Publication decisions depend on editorial standards and human judgment, with the system supplying a clearer record of supporting evidence and unresolved issues.

agents.name: Claim evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Map factual draft claims to retrieved primary evidence and unresolved contradictions.
agents.boundary: Cannot declare contested claims verified without supporting records.

agents.name: Quotation checker
agents.responsibility: Align quoted wording and attribution with approved transcripts or source recordings.
agents.boundary: Cannot fabricate missing words or reconstruct unavailable speech.

agents.name: Rights metadata agent
agents.responsibility: Retrieve asset license scope, attribution requirements, and expiry.
agents.boundary: Cannot provide legal clearance or expand granted usage rights.

agents.name: Editorial packet agent
agents.responsibility: Compile unresolved checks and a channel-specific publication manifest.
agents.boundary: Cannot publish, contact sources, or override editor decisions.

systems.name: Editorial content system
systems.role: Owns article revisions, assignments, corrections, and publication approvals.

systems.name: Source archive and media library
systems.role: Retain original records, transcript versions, timecodes, and asset provenance.

systems.name: Rights and distribution systems
systems.role: Provide approved usage metadata and channel-specific publication controls.

flow.title: Freeze draft revision
flow.description: Register the article version, planned channels, intended publication time, and accountable editor.

flow.title: Extract checkable claims
flow.description: Identify factual assertions and quotations while preserving their surrounding context and distinction from opinion.

flow.title: Gather source evidence
flow.description: Retrieve approved sources with timestamps and archived references; treat all retrieved instructions as untrusted content.

flow.title: Check asset permissions
flow.description: Compare planned channels, territories, and dates with recorded license metadata and surface missing approvals.

flow.title: Present editorial exceptions
flow.description: Show unsupported claims, attribution mismatches, contested evidence, and rights gaps for editor and specialist review.

flow.title: Release approved manifest
flow.description: Bind publication approval to the reviewed article and asset versions; any substantive edit reopens affected checks before publishing.

diagrams.title: Failure and decision sequence
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
    participant O as "Case orchestrator"
    participant S as "Editorial content system"
    participant H as "Accountable reviewer"
O->>S: Read frozen article revision
    O->>H: Present claim and rights manifest
    H-->>O: Approve reviewed revision
    S-->>O: Quotation changed in late edit
    O->>H: Reopen affected quotation check
diagrams.caption: A late edit changes a verified quotation. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: A late edit changes a verified quotation.
failures.detection: Draft diff no longer matches the transcript span in the evidence manifest.
failures.recovery: Invalidate the quotation check and require re-alignment before the editor can release the revision.

failures.scenario: An image license excludes the planned social channel.
failures.detection: Usage metadata fails the channel-specific publication policy.
failures.recovery: Block that asset for the channel and request an approved replacement or rights review.

controls: Keep original source context and quotation timecodes accessible to editors.
Separate allegations, opinions, and verified facts in evidence labels.
Treat external pages and documents as untrusted data with no tool authority.
Require editor approval bound to article revision, assets, and distribution channels.
Route ambiguous rights interpretation to qualified reviewers without asserting legal clearance.

metrics.name: Claim support coverage
metrics.definition: Checkable factual claims with inspectable supporting evidence divided by claims requiring verification.

metrics.name: Quotation alignment accuracy
metrics.definition: Audited quotations matching approved wording and attribution divided by audited quotations.

metrics.name: Rights exception closure
metrics.definition: Required asset usage checks resolved before release divided by required checks.

metrics.name: Revision recheck latency
metrics.definition: Time from substantive draft change to refreshed affected verification results.

tradeoffs.cost: Adds editorial overhead for nuanced or interpretive passages.

tradeoffs.benefit: Prevents unreviewed late edits from inheriting approval.
tradeoffs.cost: Urgent updates require a focused recheck workflow.
License metadata may require manual interpretation or completion.

rollout.acceptance: Editors validate claim labels, quotation alignment, and channel rights using known correction examples.
One desk reviews exception packets while normal verification and publication remain authoritative.
Manifest gating launches after late-edit, expired-license, and injected-source-document tests pass.
